source: Heron Landing Community Standards, Seventh Edition (October 2026)

items.title: Exterior alteration without approval
items.keywords: unapproved alteration modification addition change exterior no approval acc application permit renovation
items.observed: An exterior alteration or modification ([describe the work and where]) was observed at the property. No approved Architectural Control Committee (ACC) application is on file.
items.cure: Submit a completed Application to the Architectural Control Committee for this work, or restore the property to its previous condition, by the deadline. Do not continue the work until written Board approval is received.
items.rule: No alterations, addition or modification to a Lot or Home, or change in appearance thereof, shall be made without the prior written approval thereof being first had and obtained from the Board as required by this Declaration.

items.title: Awning
items.keywords: awning canopy lanai cover shade
items.observed: An awning was observed at [location] that has no ACC approval on file or is not on the rear of the home over the lanai in a neutral color matching the exterior.
items.cure: Remove the awning, or obtain prior Board approval. Approved awnings must be on the rear of the home over the lanai, neutral in color and matching the exterior color of the home.
items.rule: With prior Board approval, awnings are permitted on the rear of the home over the Lanai and must be neutral in color and match the exterior color of the home.

items.title: Exterior color / repainting
items.keywords: paint color repaint peeling faded stained exterior finish stone
items.observed: The exterior of the home ([describe: unapproved color / peeling or faded paint / stained]) does not meet the approved color scheme or is in need of repainting.
items.cure: Repaint the exterior in an approved community color after submitting an ACC application, or restore the previously approved color. Homes must be repainted within 45 days of notice.
items.rule: Changes to exterior of home require Board approval. All exterior colors must comply with An approved color scheme. Accent colors, not exceeding two (2) per structure, not including front door color, will be allowed. Any change of the existing color to one of the approved community color selections requires the owner to submit an application to the ACC for summary approval stating color selections. Owners wanting to repaint with existing surface colors must also submit an application to the ACC for summary approval. Stacked stone or rock alterations to a home must be approved, specifically with regard to stone color, type, finish, and texture. An owner must submit an application to the ACC for summary approval stating selection. Stone or rock alterations shall be used for accents only to the home. The exterior of Homes shall be repainted within forty-five (45) days of notice by the ACC/Board.

items.title: Fence, wall or screen enclosure
items.keywords: fence wall privacy chain link wood pvc screen enclosure screening wrought iron aluminum cage
items.observed: A [fence / wall / screen enclosure] was observed at [location] that was installed without ACC approval or is a prohibited type (wood, chain link, PVC or privacy fencing).
items.cure: Remove the fence/wall/enclosure, or replace it with an approved type after receiving written ACC approval. Only wrought iron or black aluminum fences 4' to 6' high are allowed; screen enclosures must be bronze with charcoal screening.
items.rule:
No walls or fences shall be erected without prior written review and approval. The only allowable type of fences is Wrought Iron or Black Aluminum 4’ – 6’ in height max. No wooden, chain link or PVC fences are permitted. All lots with a view of water or conservation may install a Black Aluminum fence 4’ – 6’ max in height. No privacy fencing is allowed on any lots. No chain link fencing of any kind shall be allowed. Fences shall not be installed flush to the ground so that drainage will be blocked in any way. Due to the Associations maintenance requirements and responsibilities the installation of fences within a drainage easement area is not expected to be approved. However, in the event a fence is installed within a drainage easement area, with prior written approval, the Owner is solely responsible for fence repair or replacement if the drainage easement area needs to be accessed.

All screening and screen enclosures shall have the prior written approval. All enclosures of balconies or patios, including addition of vinyl windows, shall be approved and all decks shall have the prior written approval. All screen enclosures must be bronze with charcoal screening. Homes on corner lots may be required to have landscaping on the street side of the screening or enclosure.

items.title: Fountain or sculpture
items.keywords: fountain sculpture statue water feature
items.observed: A [fountain / sculpture] was observed at [location]. Fountains and sculptures are not permitted on the property.
items.cure: Remove the fountain or sculpture from the property.
items.rule: No fountain or sculpture may be placed on the property, including in the front of the house.

items.title: Front door / entryway
items.keywords: front door entryway entry porch alcove clutter shoes trellis arbor decorative items paint color
items.observed: The front entry ([describe: unapproved door/color / more than the allowed decorative items / clutter or stored personal items]) does not comply with the Community Standards.
items.cure: Correct the entryway: obtain ACC approval for door style/color changes, limit decorative items to two (only one wall-mounted, none over 3 feet unless wall mounted), and remove stored shoes, clutter and personal items.
items.rule: Changes to front doors (door style or paint color) require approval. Front doors may be of metal, solid wood or fiberglass and may contain glass portions that may be plain, frosted or etched. Maximum of two decorative items are permitted within the alcove or porch. Items not wall mounted are not to exceed 3 feet in height. Only one item may be wall mounted. Item must be maintained in the covered entry and not extend into the walkway. Two (2) vine trellis and (1) vine arbor are permitted with approval and must not exceed 90” in height. Trellis and/or arbor material must be either metal or PVC. Trellis and/or arbor must be used in combination with living plant material. Owner must maintain such item and trim as necessary per 4.02. Entryways must be free of clutter and may not be used to store shoes or other personal items, unless specific approval has been obtained.

items.title: Garage door damaged or non-conforming
items.keywords: garage door damaged dent warped panel window carport
items.observed: The garage door has [describe: dents / warping / finish deterioration / cracked or broken panels / alignment problems / windows / non-standard design].
items.cure: Repair or replace the damaged garage door panels to the satisfaction of the Association (garage doors must be standard solid panel construction with no windows) within 30 days of notice.
items.rule: Carports, unattached garages and the screening of garage doors are not allowed in Heron Landing. All sections of garage doors, shall be of standard solid panel construction, which will conceal the contents of the garage. Garage door may NOT have windows. Garage doors shall be kept closed except when access or an activity requires them to be open. Design monograms and anything other than a solid door are not permitted, with the exception handles and other adornments originally installed by the builder. Damaged garage door panels shall be replaced (or repaired to the satisfaction of the Association) within 30 days after receiving notice from the Association. Damaged is defined as dents, warping, paint or finish deterioration, cracked/broken panels, or alignment issues.

items.title: Garage door left open
items.keywords: garage door open left open closed
items.observed: The garage door was observed open on [date(s)/time(s)] when no access or activity required it to be open.
items.cure: Keep the garage door closed except when access or an activity requires it to be open.
items.rule: Carports, unattached garages and the screening of garage doors are not allowed in Heron Landing. All sections of garage doors, shall be of standard solid panel construction, which will conceal the contents of the garage. Garage door may NOT have windows. Garage doors shall be kept closed except when access or an activity requires them to be open. Design monograms and anything other than a solid door are not permitted, with the exception handles and other adornments originally installed by the builder. Damaged garage door panels shall be replaced (or repaired to the satisfaction of the Association) within 30 days after receiving notice from the Association. Damaged is defined as dents, warping, paint or finish deterioration, cracked/broken panels, or alignment issues.

items.title: Glass block
items.keywords: glass block window
items.observed: Glass block was observed on the [home / addition]. Glass block is not permitted.
items.cure: Remove the glass block and replace it with an approved window treatment after ACC approval.
items.rule: The use of glass blocks on an existing home or the use of glass block in an addition to an existing home is not allowed within Heron Landing.

items.title: Hurricane shutters left closed
items.keywords: hurricane shutters storm panels accordion roll-up closed
items.observed: Hurricane shutters/panels were observed closed with no hurricane watch or warning in effect.
items.cure: Open or remove the hurricane shutters. Shutters may be closed only up to 72 hours before an expected hurricane and must be opened or removed within one week after the watch or warning ends.
items.rule: Any hurricane shutters or other protective devices visible from outside a Home shall be of a type as approved in writing by the ACC. Panel, accordion and roll-up style hurricane shutters may not be left closed during hurricane season (nor at any other time). Any such approved hurricane shutters may be installed or closed up to seventy-two (72) hours prior to the expected arrival of a hurricane and must be removed or opened within one (71) week after the end of a hurricane watch or warning or as the Board may determine otherwise. Except as the B o a r d may otherwise decide, shutters may not be closed at any time other than a storm event. Any approval by the ACC shall not be deemed an endorsement of the effectiveness of hurricane shutters.

items.title: Porch, deck, patio or screen enclosure
items.keywords: porch deck patio lanai screen enclosure roof mold mildew screened front porch
items.observed: A [porch / deck / patio / screen enclosure] at [location] ([describe: no ACC approval / non-compliant roof or materials / not finished to the ground / mold or mildew]) does not comply with the Community Standards.
items.cure: Obtain ACC approval for the structure or correct it to comply (consistent appearance, bronze/black aluminum with charcoal screen, compliant roof, finished to the ground and free of mold, mildew and weeds). Screened front porches are not permitted.
items.standards_title: Porches, Decks, Screen Enclosures and Patios
items.rule:
All such structures must be submitted to the ACC for its approval. All structures shall have an appearance consistent with the dwelling and the community. Any porch, patio, screen enclosures or deck shall comply with existing setback governance. Porches, screen enclosures or decks, which are constructed above ground must be finished to the ground with materials compatible with the deck or the dwelling, free of mold, mildew, weeds and may be screened with landscaping.

Screened in front porch areas are not permitted. Screen doors are allowed on front doors upon approval of the ACC.

Screen enclosures shall be constructed with bronze/black colored aluminum supports and smoke/charcoal colored screen material. Enclosures shall not exceed the width and height of the home nor extend beyond the dwelling’s existing roofline. No porches, decks, screen enclosures or patios will be allowed to have aluminum, metal, plastic or fiberglass roofs where the roof pitch is equal to or greater than 3/12 unless it will be covered by composite asphalt/fiberglass, multi-tab or dimensional shingles. Any future roof replacement costs, on approved ACC additions, shall be the responsibility of the Homeowner.

items.title: Roof repair or change
items.keywords: roof roofing shingles tiles damage leak tarp repair
items.observed: The roof ([describe: damaged or missing shingles/tiles / tarp / unapproved roofing change]) requires repair or approval.
items.cure: Complete routine roof repairs within 45 days of notice, or submit an ACC application for any roof change. If the damage resulted from a catastrophic weather event, keep management informed about insurance, warranty and contractor status so a reasonable timeline can be agreed.
items.rule: All changes to the roofing of your home will require prior approval from the ACC. Routine roof repairs need to be completed within 45 days of notice by management, unless an alternative timeline is approved. If the damage was caused due to a catastrophic weather event the Management Company and HOA board should be kept aware on the status of insurance, warranty, and/or contractor availability to show good faith in correcting roofing issues. A reasonable timeline will be agreed upon.

items.title: Satellite dish / antenna
items.keywords: satellite dish antenna mast tower aerial
items.observed: A [satellite dish / antenna / mast] was observed at [location] without ACC approval or visible from the street/neighbors.
items.cure: Remove the equipment or obtain prior ACC approval for the location and screening. Dishes over 39.37 inches are prohibited.
items.rule: No exterior visible antennae, radio masts, towers, poles, aerials, satellite dishes, or other similar equipment shall be placed on any Home or Lot without the prior written approval thereof being first had and obtained from the ACC as required by this Declaration. The ACC may require, among other things, that all such improvements be screened so that they are not visible from adjacent Homes, or from the Common Areas. Each Owner agrees that the location of such items must be first approved by the ACC in order to address the safety and welfare of the residents of Heron Landing. No Owner shall operate any equipment or device, which will interfere with the radio or television reception of others. All antennas not covered by the Federal Communications Commission ("FCC") rules are prohibited. Installation, maintenance, and use of all antennas shall comply with restrictions adopted by the Board and shall be governed by the then current rules of the FCC.

items.title: Solar equipment
items.keywords: solar panels heating equipment roof front
items.observed: Solar equipment was observed [installed without ACC approval / on the front of the home or front portion of the property].
items.cure: Remove the equipment or obtain ACC approval. Solar equipment may not be installed on the front of the home or the front portion of the property.
items.rule: The addition of any solar heating equipment must be reviewed and approved by the ACC. Solar equipment may not be installed on the front of the home or front portion of property.

items.title: Pool, spa or pool project
items.keywords: pool spa hot tub whirlpool pool cage screen torn debris sidewalk damage cleanliness above ground equipment
items.observed: [Describe: unapproved pool/spa/cage / torn or damaged pool cage screen / pool equipment not screened / debris on sidewalk or street / damaged sidewalk / lawn and beds not restored / chlorinated water discharged].
items.cure: Correct the condition: obtain ACC approval for pool work; repair or replace a damaged pool cage within 90 days; screen pool equipment with landscaping; keep sidewalks and streets clear of debris; repair community property damage and restore lawn, beds and irrigation within 30 days of completion.
items.standards_title: Swimming Pools, Spas, Whirlpools, and Hot Tubs
items.rule:
No aboveground pools shall be permitted. All in-ground pools, hot tubs, spas and appurtenances installed shall require the prior written approval of the ACC. Pools with fiberglass shells are prohibited. The design must incorporate, at a minimum, the following: (I) the composition of the material must be thoroughly tested and accepted by the industry for such construction; (ii) any swimming pool constructed on any Lot shall have an elevation at the top of the pool of not over two feet (2') above the natural grade unless approved by the ACC; (iii) pool cages must be of a design, color and material approved by the ACC; and (IV) pool cages shall in no event be higher than the roof line of the Home or more than one story. Pool cages/ patios/ outdoor living area shall not extend beyond the sides of the Home without express approval by the BOD.

All pools shall be adequately maintained and chlorinated (or cleaned with similar treatment). No diving boards, slides, or platforms s h a l l be permitted without ACC approval. Under no circumstances m a y chlorinated water be discharged onto other Owners’ lawns, the community streets, or into any water bodies within Heron Landing or adjoining properties.

Any pool cage that is damaged or if a screen is torn, the homeowner is required to correct the repair/ replace said issue within 90 days.

Pool equipment is to be shielded from view (from street and neighboring properties) with landscaping. Landscaping plan is required to be submitted to ACC for approval. Homeowner is responsible for repairing any damaged to the sidewalks or other community property as a result of said project. Repairs must take place within 30 days after substantial completion of project or pool cage is installed (whichever is earlier or relevant).

Homeowner is responsible for taking necessary actions to keep sidewalks and streets clear of debris (sand, dirt, stone, pavers, etc.) at all times until project is complete.

Lawn, flower beds and irrigation are required to be fully restored within 30 days after (whichever is applicable) either the pool cage is installed, final grading is completed, or fence is installed. Homeowner is responsible for keeping lawn and improved landscape areas maintained during pool install. Specifically:

 Landscape beds are required to be weeded  Lawn is required to be cut in accordance with 4.05 Turf  Reasonable steps must be taken to keep lawn watered if irrigation system is damaged or unavailable during the course of the project o Reasonable steps include watering via a lawn sprinkler & hose  Lawn shall be fertilized & free of weeds  Hardedges are required to be maintained

items.title: Window treatments
items.keywords: window treatment blinds drapes sheet foil newspaper tint reflective security bars signs neon rope lights
items.observed: Window treatments at [location] ([describe: temporary covering such as sheets/foil/newspaper / signs or decorative items in window / reflective tint / security bars / non-neutral color]) do not comply with the Community Standards.
items.cure: Remove the non-compliant items and use only blinds, neutral drapes or shutters. Obtain written approval before installing security bars, reflective tinting or exterior shutters/awnings.
items.rule: Window treatments shall consist of drapery, blinds, decorative panels, or other window covering, and no newspaper, aluminum foil, sheets or other temporary window treatments are permitted. No signs, clings, designs, pictures, rope lights, neon signs, statues, or other decorative items are permitted to be displayed in windows, with the exception of holiday decorations as permitted in section 3.29. Only window blinds, neutral drapes, or shutters are allowed. No security bars shall be placed on the windows of any Home without prior written approval. No awnings, canopies or shutters shall be affixed to the exterior of a Home without the prior written approval. No reflective tinting or mirror finishes on windows shall be permitted unless approved. Window treatments facing the street shall be of a neutral color, such as white, off-white or wood tones.

items.title: Window or wall air conditioner / fan
items.keywords: window air conditioner ac unit wall fan
items.observed: A [window / wall] air conditioning unit or window fan was observed at [location]. These are prohibited.
items.cure: Remove the window or wall unit/fan.
items.rule: No window, wall air conditioning unit, or window fan may be installed in any window or wall of a Home.

items.title: Air conditioning equipment unscreened
items.keywords: air conditioner ac condenser equipment screening shrubs noise
items.observed: Outdoor air conditioning equipment at [location] is not screened from view of the street and neighboring homes.
items.cure: Screen the equipment with shrubs and/or approved fencing (landscaping plan or fence application to the ACC as required).
items.rule: Outdoor air conditioning units shall be placed to minimize noise to adjacent dwellings and shall be screened from view from the street and neighboring homes with shrubs and/or approved fencing. Refer to paragraph 3.17 for fencing approval. Window air conditioner units and/ or window fans are prohibited.

items.title: Rain barrel
items.keywords: rain barrel cistern water collection
items.observed: A rain barrel was observed at [location] [without ACC approval / visible from the street / not neutral or earth-toned].
items.cure: Obtain ACC approval and store the barrel behind the home out of view from any street in a neutral or earth-tone color, or remove it.
items.rule: Rain barrels require ACC approval before installation. Rain barrels need to be stored behind the home, not visible from any street. Rain barrels must be neutral or earth-toned in color.

items.title: Water softener unscreened
items.keywords: water softener conditioner screening
items.observed: A water softener at [location] is visible from the street/neighbors and is not screened.
items.cure: Screen the water softener from view with landscaping or approved fencing.
items.rule: Water softeners are permitted outside homes but must be screened from view using landscaping or approved fencing.

items.title: Yard ornament
items.keywords: yard ornament decoration statue gnome figurine decor garden art
items.observed: [Number] yard ornament(s) ([describe]) were observed at [location] without ACC approval, or exceeding two ornaments / 36 inches in height.
items.cure: Remove the unauthorized yard ornaments within 24 hours of notice. Up to two ornaments under 36 inches tall are allowed only with prior ACC approval and only in a landscape bed.
items.rule: Maximum of two (2) yard ornaments less than 36” in height are permitted per yard and must have ACC approval prior to installation. A picture or detailed description of the item must be submitted with the request, along with the proposed location for the structure which shall be located only in a landscaping bed and must blend in with the home. The materials and color used shall be generally subdued and in harmony with the natural surroundings of the home, lot and community. No bright colors, unusual materials offensive or obscene items will be approved. Yard ornamentals may be denied for any reason without explanation. Unauthorized yard ornaments will be removed with 24- hour notice.

items.title: Damage not repaired
items.keywords: damage casualty fire storm destroyed repair rebuild
items.observed: The [home / improvement] at [location] has [describe damage] and repair or rebuilding has not been commenced.
items.cure: Commence repair or rebuilding of the damaged home or improvement in accordance with the Declaration, and provide the Association with a schedule. Notify management of the insurance status.
items.rule: In the event that a Home or other improvement is damaged or destroyed by casualty loss or other loss, then the Owner thereof shall commence to rebuild or repair the damaged Home or improvement in accordance with the Declaration. As to any such reconstruction of a destroyed Home or improvements, the same shall only be replaced as approved. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, to the extent that insurance coverage obtained and maintained by the Association covers such casualty destruction, the Owner of such damaged or destroyed Home shall not perform any activities that would negate such coverage or impair the availability of such coverage.

items.title: ATV / dirt bike
items.keywords: atv dirt bike four wheeler motorcycle off road golf cart scooter minibike
items.observed: An [ATV / dirt bike] was observed [being driven / parked or stored outside the garage] on [date].
items.cure: Store ATVs and dirt bikes in the garage and transport them out of the neighborhood on a trailer. They may not be driven anywhere in Heron Landing.
items.rule: All-terrain vehicles (ATV) and dirt bikes are not permitted to be driven anywhere in Heron Landing. They must be stored in the garage and put on a trailer to be taken out of the neighborhood.

items.title: Commercial vehicle on driveway
items.keywords: commercial vehicle work truck van lettering ladder rack driveway
items.observed: A commercial vehicle ([description / plate]) was observed parked on the driveway on [date(s)].
items.cure: Park commercial vehicles (work vehicles, vehicles with writing on the sides, or equipment racks/holders) inside the garage at all times.
items.rule: Commercial Vehicles (vehicles used for work purposes and vehicles with writing on the sides or equipment racks or holders) are not permitted to be parked on driveways in Heron Landing. They must be parked inside a garage at all times. The exception to this is a county or government issued vehicle.

items.title: Prohibited vehicle (RV, boat, trailer, camper, etc.)
items.keywords: recreational vehicle rv camper boat trailer limousine for sale sign domicile golf cart prohibited vehicle
items.observed: A [RV / camper / boat / trailer / limousine / vehicle displaying a for-sale or commercial sign] ([description / plate]) was observed parked outside a garage on [date(s)].
items.cure: Store the vehicle inside the garage, or remove it from Heron Landing. Vehicles bearing for-sale signs or commercial advertising may not be parked in public view, and no vehicle may be used as a residence.
items.rule: No commercial vehicle, limousine, recreational vehicle, all-terrain vehicle, boat, trailer, including without limitation, boat trailers, house trailers, and trailers of every other type, kind or description, or camper, may be kept within Heron Landing except in the garage of a Home. The term "commercial vehicle" shall not be deemed to include law enforcement vehicles or recreational or utility vehicles (i.e., Broncos, Blazers, Explorers, Navigators, etc.) or clean "non-working" vehicles such as pick-up trucks, vans, or cars if they are used by the Owner on a daily basis for normal transportation; provided, however, vehicles with ladders, racks, and hooks attached to such vehicles shall be "commercial vehicles" prohibited by this Section. No vehicles displaying commercial advertising shall be parked within the public view. No vehicles bearin g a "for sale" sign shall be parked within the public view anywhere within Heron Landing. For any Owner who drives an automobile issued by the County or other governmental entity (i.e., police cars), such automobile shall not be deemed to be a commercial vehicle and may be parked in the garage or driveway of the Lot. No vehicle shall be used as a domicile or residence either temporarily or permanently. No gas powered: all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), golf carts, scooters or mini motorcycles are permitted at any time on any paved surfaces or Common Areas. Additionally, no ATV, golf cart or mini motorcycle may be parked or stored within Heron Landing, including any Lot, except in the garage of a Home. Notwithstanding any other provision in this Declaration to the contrary, the foregoing restrictions shall not apply to construction vehicles utilized in connection with construction, improvement, installation, or repair by Declarant, or its agents.

items.title: Trailer in public view
items.keywords: trailer flat bed cargo horse motorcycle boat rv public view
items.observed: A trailer ([type]) was observed in public view at [location] on [date(s)].
items.cure: Store the trailer in the garage and keep the garage door closed.
items.rule: Trailers (flat bed, cargo, horse, motorcycle, boat, RVs, etc.) are not permitted in public view in Heron Landing. Trailers must be stored in garages and garages must remain closed.

items.title: Watercraft not stored in garage
items.keywords: boat jet ski canoe kayak watercraft paddleboard
items.observed: [Boat / jet ski / canoe / kayak] was observed stored outside the garage at [location].
items.cure: Store boats, jet skis, canoes, kayaks and other water equipment only inside the garage.
items.rule: Boats, jet skis, canoes, kayaks and water equipment are to be stored only in garages.

items.title: Vehicle repair / inoperable vehicle
items.keywords: vehicle repair inoperable blocks tarp cover jack engine maintenance driveway
items.observed: [Describe: vehicle that cannot operate on its own power for more than 12 hours / vehicle repair or maintenance in the driveway / vehicle on blocks / tarp-covered vehicle] at [location].
items.cure: Move the vehicle into the garage. Vehicles that cannot operate on their own power may not remain more than 12 hours except in a garage; repairs (other than emergency repairs) must be done in a garage, and vehicles may not be stored on blocks or covered with tarps in public view.
items.rule: No vehicle, which cannot operate on its own power shall remain in Heron Landing for more than twelve (12) hours, except in the garage of a Home. No repair or maintenance, except emergency repair, of vehicles shall be made within Heron Landing, except in the garage of a Home. Repairing vehicles in a driveway is prohibited at all times. No vehicles shall be stored on blocks. No tarpaulin covers on vehicles shall be permitted anywhere within the public view.

items.title: Vehicle parked on street overnight
items.keywords: overnight street parking parked in street curb
items.observed: A vehicle ([description / plate]) was observed parked on the street overnight on [date(s)].
items.cure: Park vehicles in the garage or driveway. Parking on the street overnight is not allowed.
items.rule:
All vehicles must be properly licensed with tags clearly displayed. No unlicensed vehicles are permitted on any paved area within the community. Owners' automobiles shall be parked in the garage or driveway and shall not block the sidewalk. Residents are not allowed to park their vehicles in the street overnight. Any damaged vehicles must be stored inside the garage. A damaged vehicles is defined as any of the following:  Has sustained significant damage to its body, frame, or mechanical components, making it

unsafe or inoperable.  Is visibly dented, rusted, or otherwise in a state of disrepair.  Has been declared a total loss by an insurance company.  Emits excessive noise or smoke, or has other issues that affect its normal operation.

No vehicles of any kind shall be parked on any portion of Heron Landing or a Lot except on the surfaced parking area thereof. Vehicles shall not park on the paved surfaces comprising the Common Area. To the extent Heron Landing has any guest parking, Owners are prohibited from parking in such guest parking spaces. No vehicles used in business for the purpose of transporting goods, equipment and the like, shall be parked in Heron Landing except during the period of delivery. Campers, boats, and motorcycles must be parked inside garages at all times. No loud vehicles or vehicles emitting obnoxious odors are permitted.

items.title: Vehicle on grass, common area or guest parking
items.keywords: parked on lawn grass common area guest parking
items.observed: A vehicle ([description / plate]) was observed parked on [the lawn / common area paved surface / a guest parking space] on [date(s)].
items.cure: Park only in the garage or on the driveway. Owners may not park on lawns, on the paved Common Area or in guest parking spaces.
items.rule:
All vehicles must be properly licensed with tags clearly displayed. No unlicensed vehicles are permitted on any paved area within the community. Owners' automobiles shall be parked in the garage or driveway and shall not block the sidewalk. Residents are not allowed to park their vehicles in the street overnight. Any damaged vehicles must be stored inside the garage. A damaged vehicles is defined as any of the following:  Has sustained significant damage to its body, frame, or mechanical components, making it

unsafe or inoperable.  Is visibly dented, rusted, or otherwise in a state of disrepair.  Has been declared a total loss by an insurance company.  Emits excessive noise or smoke, or has other issues that affect its normal operation.

No vehicles of any kind shall be parked on any portion of Heron Landing or a Lot except on the surfaced parking area thereof. Vehicles shall not park on the paved surfaces comprising the Common Area. To the extent Heron Landing has any guest parking, Owners are prohibited from parking in such guest parking spaces. No vehicles used in business for the purpose of transporting goods, equipment and the like, shall be parked in Heron Landing except during the period of delivery. Campers, boats, and motorcycles must be parked inside garages at all times. No loud vehicles or vehicles emitting obnoxious odors are permitted.

items.title: Equipment stored outside
items.keywords: equipment stored outside lawn care car care tools ladder mower work equipment
items.observed: [Lawn care / car care / work] equipment ([describe]) was observed stored outside the residence at [location].
items.cure: Store all equipment inside the residence or garage, out of view.
items.rule: Equipment (i.e., lawn care, car care, work equipment, etc.) is not permitted to be stored outside of the residence.

items.title: Garbage cans visible / not shielded
items.keywords: garbage can trash can bin bins waste container visible shielded screened side of house smell odor rodents
items.observed: Garbage/trash cans were observed at [location] visible from the street or neighboring homes and not shielded from view.
items.cure: Store garbage cans inside the garage or on the side of the home fully shielded from view, with lids secured. To use an outside location, submit a plan to the ACC to shield the cans (at least 80% screened with tall/mature plants at first, fully screened within 12 months).
items.rule:
Trash collection and disposal procedures established by Association shall be observed. No outside burning of trash or garbage is permitted at any time. No garbage cans supplies, or other similar articles shall be maintained on any Lot so as to be visible from outside the Home or Lot. Each Owner shall be responsible for properly depositing garbage and trash in garbage cans and trash

containers sufficient for pick-up by the appropriate collection agencies in accordance with the requirements of any such agency.

If trash cans are stored outside, residents must take care to properly secure cans from rodents and ensure no foul orders impact surrounding homes. Trash receptacles shall be maintained in a sanitary condition and shall be shielded from the view of adjacent properties and streets. Trash cans may be stored outside, on the side of the residence and shielded from view. Residents must submit plans to shield trash cans from view to obtain approval. Initially garbage can must be at least 80% covered (shielded from view) with tall/ mature plants. The remaining coverage must be filled in within 12 months. If not, homeowner is required to plant larger plants to cover garbage can completely.

Garbage cans and trash containers shall not be placed outside the Home for pick-up earlier than 5:00 p.m. on the day preceding the pick-up and shall return all containers to their concealed location no later 10:00 p.m. the day of pick-up. Trashcan lids should be secured to avoid animals, odor, and windblown garbage from affecting adjoining homes. Each resident is responsible for picking up litter on their property and preventing windblown debris from originating from their property.

No trash of any kind can be stored in plain view. Any trash on property needs to be removed from view.
