items.title: Garden hose / reel
items.keywords: garden hose reel hanger retracted coiled
items.observed: Garden hose(s) were observed [left unrolled on the ground / on a non-neutral colored reel or hanger / visible from the street] at [location].
items.cure: Fully retract and neatly hang hoses when not in use. Hangers, reels and hoses must be placed on the side of the home, concealed from the street, and in neutral colors (dark green, brown, black, earth tones).
items.rule: Garden hose hangers or hose reels should be placed on the side of the Home and concealed from the street. Hoses must be fully retracted and hung neatly when not in use. Hangers, hose reels and hoses must be neutral in color (dark green, brown, black, earthtones).

items.title: Grill
items.keywords: grill bbq barbecue cooker outdoor cooking
items.observed: A grill was observed [uncovered / stored in front of the home or visible from the street / in use on common area] at [location].
items.cure: Cover the grill and store it behind the home on the patio/lanai when not in use. No cooking is permitted on the Common Areas.
items.rule: Grills must be covered and stored behind the home on patio when not in use. No cooking shall be permitted nor shall any goods or beverages be consumed on the Common Areas, except in areas designated for those purposes by Association. The Board shall have the right to prohibit or restrict the use of grills or barbecue facilities throughout Heron Landing.

items.title: Laundry / rugs visible
items.keywords: laundry clothes towels rugs mops hanging drying visible
items.observed: Laundry, rugs or similar items were observed hung or exposed at [location], visible from outside the home or lot.
items.cure: Remove laundry, rugs, mops and similar articles from view.
items.rule: Subject to the provisions of Section 163.04 of the Florida Statutes, to the extent applicable, no rugs, mops, or laundry of any kind, or any other similar type article, shall be shaken, hung or exposed so as to be visible outside the Home or Lot.

items.title: Patio / lanai furniture, indoor furniture or appliances
items.keywords: patio furniture lanai front porch indoor furniture appliance couch refrigerator driveway
items.observed: [Indoor furniture / a full-size appliance / furniture on the driveway / non-neutral or unapproved front furniture] was observed at [location].
items.cure: Remove the item. Indoor furniture and household appliances may not be placed in front yards, patios, gardens or flowerbeds; no furniture is allowed on driveways; front-area furniture requires ACC approval and must be neutral outdoor furniture.
items.rule: Patio or Lanai furniture located in the front of the home requires ACC approval. The only acceptable furniture for patios, lanais and front porch areas is neutral outdoor furniture. Outdoor grills shall be restricted to rear lanai/patio. Indoor furniture or full-size household appliances of any type shall not be placed or stored in front yards, back patios, gardens or flowerbeds of homes. No furniture of any type is allowed on driveways.

items.title: Fuel / propane tank / hazardous substances
items.keywords: propane tank fuel gasoline flammable hazardous chemical gas bottle
items.observed: [Propane tank / fuel / flammable or hazardous substance] was observed at [location] [visible / stored outside normal household use].
items.cure: Install propane and bottled gas tanks underground or screen them from view with ACC-approved landscaping or materials, and remove any flammable, combustible or hazardous substances beyond normal household use.
items.rule: No flammable, combustible or explosive fuel, fluid, chemical, hazardous waste, or substance shall be kept on any portion of Heron Landing or within any Home or Lot, except those which are required for normal household u s e . All propane tanks a n d bottled gas for household and/o r pool purposes (excluding barbecue grill tanks) must be installed underground or in a manner to be screened from view by landscaping or other materials approved by the ACC.

items.title: Temporary storage container (POD)
items.keywords: pod storage container dumpster temporary container pod unit
items.observed: A temporary storage container/POD was observed at [location] since [date] [without notifying the Association / beyond 14 days / blocking the sidewalk or roadway].
items.cure: Remove the container. Only one container is allowed, for no more than 14 days, not blocking the sidewalk or roadway, and the Association must be notified of the arrival and pick-up dates.
items.rule: Only one POD unit or other temporary storage containers are allowed at a residence no longer than 14 days and must not be placed where it interferes with the sidewalk or roadway. Residents wishing to have a temporary storage container must notify the Association when the container will arrive and be picked up. Extensions to the 14-day period will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

items.title: Temporary structure / tent
items.keywords: temporary structure tent gazebo canopy pop up shed trailer building
items.observed: A temporary [structure / tent / gazebo / building] was observed at [location] on [date(s)].
items.cure: Remove the structure. Pop-up tents and gazebos may be used only temporarily for events and may not be stored in yards or used regularly.
items.rule: No structure of a temporary character, trailer, tent, or other building is permitted. Pop-up Canvas type tents or gazebos are permitted only when in use temporarily (for events, parties, gatherings) and may not be stored in yards or used regularly. Residents wishing to have a temporary structure must notify the Association when the container will arrive and be picked up.

items.title: Exterior lighting (bulbs, fixtures)
items.keywords: exterior lighting coach light bulb burnt out fixture yellow color flashing mismatched
items.observed: Exterior lighting at [location] ([describe: burnt-out or damaged bulb / mismatched bulbs / colored or flashing bulbs / damaged, broken or missing fixture]) does not comply with the Community Standards.
items.cure: Replace damaged or burnt-out bulbs within one week; use matching clear or frosted bulbs of the same wattage and lumens (no colored or flashing bulbs outside the winter holiday season); repair or replace damaged fixtures with matching bronze or black fixtures upon notice.
items.rule: Changes to exterior lighting of home require approval. Coach Lights must be the same or very similar to the lights already installed (all light fixtures must match). Lights must be bronze or black in color with clear glass. All fixtures must match and be in good condition (not showing signs of wear). Light fixtures must be proportionate to home. Lights must be mounted to home, left and right of garage door. Minimum height from ground to the bottom of fixture is 6 feet. Bulbs may be clear or frosted. Yellow or any other color bulbs are not approved except during the winter holiday season. In no event shall a resident have a combination of light bulbs (all bulbs must be of the same wattage & same lumens). No flashing or flickering bulbs are allowed. Damaged or burnt-out bulbs must be replaced within one (1) week. Damaged, broken or missing light fixtures must be replaced upon notice from the Association. Homeowner must obtain approval for new coach lights.

items.title: Garden / walkway lighting
items.keywords: garden light walkway landscape lighting low voltage wires
items.observed: Garden/walkway lighting at [location] was installed without approval or does not meet the standards (height, bulb, wires visible, placement).
items.cure: Remove the lights or obtain ACC approval. Lights must be in existing beds, 12 inches or less, with white 4/7/11 watt bulbs, concealed wires, not reflecting into adjacent homes.
items.rule: Any lighting requires approval. Low voltage garden lights permitted on the home site but only in existing flower and shrubbery beds, and only on a conditional basis. Approval may be rescinded if installation is not maintained. Lights may be placed no closer than eight inches to the edge of the bed. Lights shall not exceed twelve (12) inches in height, with white bulbs of 4, 7 or 11 watts. Lights shall be installed in a manner consistent with the purpose intended, shall not reflect into adjacent homes, and shall be maintained at all times by Homeowner. Light wires must be concealed and not visible

items.title: Generator
items.keywords: generator propane standby
items.observed: A generator was observed at [location] without written approval, or [used outside a power outage / unscreened].
items.cure: Remove the generator or obtain written approval, permits and screening. Permanent propane generators may be used only during power outages.
items.rule: Permanently installed external propane generators may be allowed. All specifications including size, type, location, appropriate screening, etc., must be approved in writing. Local, county & state applicable permits and approvals will be required. Such generators would only be allowed to be used during periods of electric power outages. See Appendix B for more information.

items.title: Holiday decorations left up
items.keywords: holiday decorations christmas halloween lights inflatable removed after season extension cords
items.observed: [Holiday/seasonal] decorations ([describe]) were observed on [date], outside the permitted display period.
items.cure: Remove the decorations, lights, extension cords and clips. Decorations may be displayed no earlier than 15 days before and must be removed no later than 7 days after a holiday; fall decorations Oct 1 - Dec 1; winter decorations 3 weeks before Thanksgiving until Jan 15. Light displays may not emit sound.
items.rule: Decorations may be displayed no earlier than 15 days prior to and must then be removed no later than 7 days after a holiday. These holidays include: Halloween, Valentine’s Day, Easter and Independence Day. Fall decorations may be displayed no earlier than October 1 and must be removed no later than December 1st. Winter/Holiday decorations may be displayed three (3) weeks prior to Thanksgiving and must be removed no later than January 15th of the following year. Care should be taken when deciding on placement of yard decorations, noting that large snow globes or inflatables may cause dead spots in lawns. All lighting, lighting accessories, extension cords and light clips and decorations shall be totally removed by January 15th. In no circumstance shall light display have or emit any sound.

items.title: House numbers missing or non-compliant
items.keywords: house number missing address numbers
items.observed: House numbers are [missing / not clearly readable from the street / not black, non-reflective and 4-6 inches].
items.cure: Install black, non-reflective house numbers 4 to 6 inches in height, clearly readable from the street, within 14 days of notice.
items.rule: All house numbers must be clearly readable from the street, but not so large as to be out of proportion to the structure, and compatibility to the overall design of the structure. Numbers are required to be black, non-reflective, and between 4-6 inches in height. All missing house numbers must be replaced by the homeowner within 14-day notice from the Association.

items.title: Painted curb numbers
items.keywords: curb numbers painted address
items.observed: Numbers were painted on the curb at [location]. Painted curb numbers are not permitted.
items.cure: Remove the painted numbers and restore the curb to its original condition.
items.rule: Heron Landing does not permit painted numbers on curbs.

items.title: Security lighting
items.keywords: security light floodlight motion night nuisance
items.observed: Security lighting at [location] [was installed without meeting the standards / was left on through the night / illuminates neighboring homes].
items.cure: Correct the lighting: simple lamp holders under the eave only (no wall mounting), motion-activated, aimed away from neighbors, and not left on throughout the night; or remove them.
items.rule: Security lights mounted on the home are permitted under the following conditions: Homeowner shall obtain and pay for all permits if required by local authority having jurisdiction. Security lights shall be of the simple lamp holder type and not a decorative luminary. Mount holder to the metal soffit under the eave or rake on the roof. Wall mounting not permitted. Maximum of two lamps per holder in any one location. Maximum of four locations on home. Maximum wattage per lamp shall be 100 incandescent. Lamps shall be aimed so as not to illuminate neighbor's homes. Lights shall be turned on by means of a motion detector or other security breach detector. Security Lights may not be left on throughout the night. Homeowner will have to remove if lighting becomes a nuisance to neighboring properties.

items.title: Eave / soffit lighting
items.keywords: eave soffit lighting govee hue led strip lights colors dangling cords
items.observed: Eave/soffit lighting at [location] [lacks ACC approval / has dangling cords or visible wires / is colored or on past 10 p.m. outside holiday periods].
items.cure: Obtain written ACC approval, secure all wires and cords flush and concealed (dangling cords within seven days), keep lights white outside holidays, and turn them off by 10 p.m.
items.rule:
All lighting to be installed on the eaves or soffit of a home must have written ACC approval. This includes temporary or "permanent" lighting including but not limited to Govee or Phillips Hue type lights. Lights

must be installed in a manner which makes all lights and wires flush with the soffit/eave of the home. Any cords which are found to be dangling or hanging from the eave must be corrected by the homeowner within seven (7) days. All wires, lights, plugs and/or electrical cords must be flush to the home and/or properly concealed in a manner which does not leave them visible from the street or neighbors home. Consistent with other rules contained here-in, during non-holiday periods the lights must remain white in color and cannot be left on past 10pm. Lights cannot impact another property or be a nuisance to any other neighbor. Lights may match minor holiday colors (St. Patrick's Day) and/or event related colors such as Super Bowl only on the day preceding and day of the holiday and/or event.

items.title: Sign, flag or banner
items.keywords: sign flag banner flagpole political for sale advertisement lettering
items.observed: A [sign / flag / banner] ([describe]) was observed at [location], visible from the outside.
items.cure: Remove the item. Only the permitted U.S., Florida and military/POW-MIA flags (up to 4.5' x 6') and one compliant flagpole (up to 20 feet) are allowed.
items.rule:
No sign, flag, banner, advertisement, notice or other lettering shall be exhibited, displayed, inscribed, painted or affixed in, or upon any part of Heron Landing, including without limitation, any Home or Lot, that is visible from the outside; provided, however, any Owner may display in a respectful manner one (1) portable, removable United States flag or official flag of the State of Florida and one (1) portable, removable official flag of the United States Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard, or a POW-MIA flag. Any such permitted flags may not exceed four and one-half feet (4') by six feet (6').

Each Owner may erect one (1) freestanding flagpole that is no more than twenty feet (20') high on any portion of such Owner’s Lot if the flagpole does not obstruct sightlines at intersections and is not erected within or upon any easement. The flagpole may not be installed any closer than ten feet (10') from the back of curb, or within ten feet (10') of any Lot line. Any Owner may further display from the flagpole, one (1) official United States flag, not larger than four and one-half feet (4') by six feet (6') and may additionally display one (1) official flag of the State of Florida or the United States Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Coast Guard, or a POW-MIA flag. Such additional flag must be equal in size to or smaller than the United States flag. Any flag pole installed in accordance with this Section is subject to all building codes, zoning setbacks, and other applicable governmental regulations, including without limitation noise and lighting ordinances in the County or municipality in which the flag pole is erected and all setback and location criteria contained in this Declaration.

Declarant is exempt from this Section; provided, further, the Declarant specifically reserves the right, for itself and its agents, employees, nominees and assigns the right, privilege and easement to construct, place and maintain upon any property within Heron Landing such signs as it deems appropriate in connection with the development, improvement, construction, marketing and sale of any of the Lots. The prohibitions on signs displayed on or within vehicles contained above in this Section shall not apply to commercial vehicles such as for construction use or providing pick-up and delivery services and other commercial services.

items.title: Yard sale / personal event
items.keywords: yard sale garage sale event signs
items.observed: A personal yard sale/event was observed [or advertised with signs] at [location] on [date].
items.cure: Cease the sale and remove any signage. Personal events are not permitted; the community holds two events each year.
items.rule: No personal events are permitted. The Community may at its discretion hold two (2) events each year (spring and fall). Property Management will coordinate these events with volunteers. Signage will be placed on common areas. No signage will be placed on individual property.

items.title: Pet rule violation
items.keywords: pet dog cat animal leash waste poop tied out barking dog run unattended animals
items.observed: [Describe: pet off leash / pet tied out or left unattended outside / pet waste not picked up / more than two pets / dog run, pen or doghouse / pet in a water body] at [location] on [date].
items.cure: Comply with Section 3.02: keep pets on a leash or within an enclosed yard, never tie them out or leave them unattended outside, keep no more than two pets, remove any dog run/pen/house, pick up all pet waste immediately, and keep pets out of water bodies.
items.rule: No animals of any kind shall be raised, bred or kept within Heron Landing for commercial purposes. Other than swine, poultry, vicious breeds and uninsurable pets (i.e., pets that create policy coverage exclusions under insurance policies purchased by the Association or pets that cause increases in insurance policy premiums under insurance policies purchased by the Association), Owners may keep a maximum of two (2) pets/animals as long as such pets or animals do not constitute a nuisance. Notwithstanding the foregoing, pets may be kept or harbored in a home only so long as such pet or animals do not constitute a nuisance. A determination by the Board that an animal or pet kept or harbored in a home is a nuisance shall be conclusive and binding on all parties. All pets shall be walked on a leash. No pet shall be permitted outside a home unless such pet is kept on a leash or within an enclosed portion of the yard of a Lot or dog park. No pet or animal shall be “tied out” on the exterior of the home or in the common areas or left unattended in a yard or on a balcony, porch or patio. No dog runs, dog pens or dog houses are permitted on any Lot. When notice of removal of any pet is given by the Board, the pet shall be removed within forty-eight (48) hours of giving of the notice. All Pets shall defecate only in the “pet walking” areas within Heron Landing designated for such purpose, if any, or on the Owner’s Lot. The person walking the pet or the Owner shall clean up all matter created by the pet during the walk. Each owner shall be responsible for the activities of their pet. Pets are not permitted in any water body in Heron Landing. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, service dogs shall not be governed by the restriction contained in this Sections. The Association intends to enforce all pet related violations but will not be held liable for owners that choose to ignore attempts to get into compliance.

items.title: Nuisance
items.keywords: nuisance noise odor unsightly offensive disturbance
items.observed: [Describe the nuisance activity or condition] was observed at [location] on [date(s)].
items.cure: Cease the activity or correct the condition that constitutes a nuisance to neighbors.
items.rule: No obnoxious, unpleasant, unsightly or offensive activities shall be carried on, nor may anything be done, which can be reasonably construed to constitute a nuisance, public or private in nature. Any questions with regard to the interpretation of this section shall be decided by the BOD, whose decisions shall be final.

items.title: Rental of home (see Declaration)
items.keywords: rental rent tenant lease airbnb short term vacation
items.observed: [Describe the observed rental activity].
items.cure: Comply with the rental provisions of the Declaration. (Section 3.42 refers to the Declaration: confirm the specific requirement before issuing.)
items.rule: REFER TO THE DECLARATIONS

items.title: Basketball hoop
items.keywords: basketball hoop backboard rim net portable street hoop
items.observed: A basketball hoop at [location] [lacks ACC approval / is one of more than one / is wall mounted / is in disrepair (peeling paint, rust, damaged backboard, yellowing, damaged rim or net) / is used in the street or after 9 p.m. / is weighted with rocks or bricks].
items.cure: Correct the issue: submit an ACC request (one hoop only, no wall mounting, backboard no larger than 60 inches), repair or replace a hoop in disrepair within 7 days, do not use it in the street or after 9 p.m., and fill the base only per the manufacturer's instructions.
items.rule:
A resident may have no more than one (1) basketball hoop; portable or direct burial in-ground. No matter which type is selected, an ACC request must be submitted. ACC request must include the following: picture of hoop, model, photo/map of where hoop will be located. No-wall mounted basketball hoops are permitted. Backboard cannot be bigger than 60 inches.

The basketball hoop must be maintained & in good repair. If not, it must be replaced within 7 days. For instance, basketball hoops cannot have peeling paint, visible rust, damaged backboards, yellow/ yellowing backboards, damaged rim or damaged netting.

Basketball hoops must not cover or impede any common area or sidewalk (including while using the basketball hoop), must not be used after 9pm and must be stored inside during high wind events (portable units only). Basketball hoops may not be used in the street.

For portable hoops, no rocks/ stones/ bricks, bag of sand (or similar) maybe used to hold unit down. The base of the basketball hoop must be internally filled in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions (often with sand/ water).

items.title: Bird house / feeder
items.keywords: bird house birdhouse feeder
items.observed: A bird house/feeder at [location] [is not approved / is not in the rear yard / exceeds the size or height limits / is not maintained].
items.cure: Remove the bird house/feeder, or bring it into compliance (one only, rear yard, at least 5 feet from the property line, no higher than 6 feet, within size limits) with ACC approval.
items.rule: One birdhouse and/or bird feeder will be permitted on a revocable and conditional annual basis. If the house or feeder is not maintained or otherwise becomes offensive, the ACC/Board has the authority to rescind approval at any time and to require removal of the house or feeder. Birdhouse or feeder may be placed in the rear yard only and may be ground supported or suspended/mounted in a tree. The proposed location shall be at least 5 feet from the property line. If the home site is a corner lot, house or feeder may be located in the side yard common with the street right of way, not closer than 16 feet to the street pavement adjacent to the side yard and not closer than 40 feet to the street pavement adjacent to the front yard. House or feeder may not be suspended from a "street tree" on a corner lot. Ground supported, or tree suspended/mounted birdhouses or feeders may not be higher than 6 feet from the ground to the top of the house or feeder. The Committee will consider the size and appearance of the birdhouse or bird feeder as appropriate to the location on a one by one basis, but in no case shall the total of width plus height plus depth of a birdhouse exceed 50 inches, with maximum dimension of 18 inches, any one side or shall the total of width plus height plus depth of a bird feeder exceed 30 inches, with maximum dimension of 18 inches, any one side. If a ground supported birdhouse or bird feeder is not located in an existing planting bed, then the homeowner shall provide and maintain a mulched area at least 2 feet in diameter at the base of the support.

items.title: Clothesline
items.keywords: clothesline clothes line drying
items.observed: A clothesline at [location] is visible from the street or neighbors or remains up when not in use.
items.cure: Remove the clothesline when not in use and keep it in the rear of the lot out of view of the street and neighbors.
items.rule: Clotheslines may be installed in the rear of a Lot so long as not visible from the street or visible to your neighbors; provided, that, any such clothes line shall be removed when it is not in use as a clothes line

items.title: Play structure
items.keywords: play structure swing set playset canopy torn jungle gym
items.observed: A play structure at [location] [lacks ACC approval / exceeds 12 feet / is made of metal tubing / has a ripped or torn canopy / is not maintained / is not buffered].
items.cure: Correct the issue: obtain ACC approval, maintain the structure, and replace torn canopies with an approved earth-tone canopy within 14 days. Play sets may not exceed 12 feet and must be wood or recycled plastic.
items.rule:
The overall height of play sets may not exceed twelve (12) feet in height. Play structures must be crafted in wood or recycled plastic. Aluminum or metal tubing is prohibited. A picture and dimensions of the play set must be submitted with the architectural application prior to approval. All play sets must be maintained. Canopies must be of earth-toned colors (i.e., tan, green, olive or brown). Any ripped or torn canopies must be replaced with approved style/ color within 14 days. Applications for play structures must include a site plan clearly showing its intended placement. The structure’s visual impact to neighboring home sites and/or the street must be buffered as much as possible with approved fencing or landscaping. Fence applications must be submitted in advance of installation of the fence and only current approved styles are permitted.

If the play structure will be buffered by landscape, the plant material must start at a height of thirty- six (36) inches from the ground and may not exceed seventy-two (72) inches of overall height at maturity. The landscape buffer must be maintained at a height of 72 inches at all times. The landscape buffer installation may not alter the drainage of the home site. The proposed plant material and location of landscape buffer must be submitted to the committee via application prior to installation.

items.title: Sports / recreational equipment
items.keywords: sports equipment recreational playground skateboard ramp tree platform goal
items.observed: [Sports / recreational equipment] ([describe]) was observed at [location] without ACC approval or left outside visible from the street.
items.cure: Remove the equipment, or obtain ACC approval and buffer it with approved landscaping/fencing. Temporary sports equipment must be stored inside when not in use.
items.rule:
No recreational, playground or sports equipment shall be installed or placed within or about any

portion of Heron Landing without prior written consent of the ACC. No basketball backboards, skateboard ramps, trampolines or play structures will be permitted without the prior written approval by the ACC. Tree platforms of a similar nature shall not be constructed on any part of a Lot. Rules and Regulations governing basketball hoops may be adopted by the Association from time to time. Trampolines or sports equipment that is stored in the backyard but is visible from the street must be buffered by approved landscaping or an approved privacy fence (Please refer to fence standards). Temporary sports equipment must be stored inside when not in use.

items.title: Trampoline
items.keywords: trampoline net netting
items.observed: A trampoline at [location] [lacks ACC approval / is visible from the street or neighbors / is not secured or has damaged netting].
items.cure: Obtain ACC approval, locate the trampoline in the rear where it is not visible from any street or neighboring home, secure it, and repair damaged netting.
items.rule: Trampolines require approval. They must be located in the rear of a home and must not be visible from any street or neighboring home. Trampolines must be adequately secured to the ground & any netting must be maintained/ repaired when damaged.

items.title: Artificial vegetation
items.keywords: artificial grass turf plants flowers fake plastic
items.observed: Artificial [grass / plants / flowers] was observed at [location].
items.cure: Remove all artificial grass, plants and flowers from the exterior of the lot. Artificial turf and plastic or artificial flowers are not permitted.
items.rule: Except as otherwise permitted by Florida law, no artificial grass, plants or other artificial vegetation, or other landscape devices, shall be placed or maintained upon the exterior portion of any lot, unless approved by the Board.

items.title: Fruit tree
items.keywords: fruit tree citrus orange lemon mango fruit bearing
items.observed: A fruit-bearing tree ([type]) was observed at [location].
items.cure: Remove the fruit-bearing tree. Fruit-bearing trees of any kind are not permitted.
items.rule: No fruit bearing trees or any kind are permitted.

items.title: Potted plants
items.keywords: potted plants flowerpot pots empty weeds driveway front
items.observed: Potted plants at [location] [exceed the limits (3 in the driveway area / 5 in front) / are empty, bare or contain weeds / are not maintained].
items.cure: Reduce the number of pots to the permitted limits, and keep every pot planted with approved, healthy plants and free of weeds.
items.rule:
Decorative potted plants are limited to three (3) within the driveway area of the property and a total of five (5) for the entire front portion of the property. Any potted plant must be maintained in good repair. A decorative potted plant is defined as; a plant that has been placed with soil in a decorative flowerpot, that is made of clay, ceramic, or plastic and is kept for display and decoration.

Approved flowerpots must have approved flowers & cannot be empty, bare, or contain weeds. Must be in approved condition as presented in approved ARC application.

items.title: Vegetable garden
items.keywords: vegetable garden fruit vegetables plants raised bed
items.observed: A vegetable/fruit garden at [location] [lacks ACC approval / is not in the rear of the home / is not screened from view / has plants over 6 feet or weeds].
items.cure: Remove the garden or obtain ACC approval; gardens must be in the back of the home, screened from view, maintained, weeded, and no plants may exceed 6 feet.
items.rule: Any type of fruit or vegetable producing plant must be submitted to the ACC prior to planting. No plants may exceed 6 ft.; plants must be weeded and maintained. All gardens must be in back of home and screened from view.

items.title: Obstruction of visibility on corner
items.keywords: visibility corner intersection sight line obstruction hedge
items.observed: A [hedge / shrub / object] at [location] obstructs visibility at the street intersection.
items.cure: Trim or remove the obstruction so that sight lines for drivers and pedestrians are clear (plants within 10 feet of a driveway edge or intersection must not exceed 30 inches).
items.rule: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in these restrictions, no obstruction to visibility at street intersections shall be permitted and such visibility clearances shall be maintained as required by the Board and governmental agencies. No vehicles, objects, fences, walls, hedges, shrubs or other planting shall be placed or permitted o n a corner Lot where such obstruction would create a traffic problem.

items.title: Irrigation staining / watering schedule
items.keywords: irrigation sprinkler staining rust watering schedule water restrictions
items.observed: [Staining caused by irrigation on a home, structure or paved area / watering outside the Sarasota County schedule] was observed at [location].
items.cure: Treat and remove irrigation staining, and follow the Sarasota County watering schedule.
items.rule:
Due to water quality, irrigation systems may cause staining on Homes, other structures or paved areas. It is each Owner's responsibility to treat and remove any such staining.

Homeowners are required to abide by Sarasota County watering schedule. The schedule is subject to change and is available on the County website. Additional watering restrictions and/or schedules can be implemented from time to time by the Board.

items.title: Wetland / conservation area vegetation removed
items.keywords: wetland conservation vegetation cut removal spraying swfwmd preserve
items.observed: Vegetation in the wetland/conservation area behind [address] appears to have been [cut / sprayed / removed].
items.cure: Cease cutting, spraying or removing vegetation in wetland or conservation areas. Contact the Association. The homeowner is responsible for any resulting fine from SWFWMD once the responsible party is established.
items.rule: Owners having homes adjoining wetlands or conservation areas are hereby put on notice that the cutting or removal of any vegetation in these areas is strictly prohibited. Answers to any questions about wetlands or conservation areas should be referred to the Association. In the event that the HOA is fined by SWFWMD due to the cutting, spraying or removal of any vegetation said fine shall be passed on to and paid by the homeowner. Once proven that the homeowner/resident is responsible for the cited violation.

items.title: Gutters / drainage
items.keywords: gutter downspout drainage fascia soffit stained debris water runoff
items.observed: [Gutters/fascia/soffits stained or with debris / a downspout directing water onto common area or a neighboring property] at [location].
items.cure: Clean the gutters, fascia and soffits, and redirect downspouts so they do not direct water onto common areas or neighboring property.
items.rule: Roof gutters and downspouts of six (6) or seven (7) inch aluminum construction are permitted within the approved color scheme.. Downspouts shall not direct water onto common areas or neighboring property and must drain according to approved drainage plan. Gutters, facia, or soffits must remain clean and free of stains and debris.

items.title: Driveway condition
items.keywords: driveway stain grease oil weeds pavers debris reflectors surface
items.observed: The driveway at [location] has [oil/grease/other stains / weeds growing through the pavers / debris / unapproved surface application / reflectors].
items.cure: Clean the stains, remove weeds and debris, and remove any reflectors or unapproved surface applications. Driveway changes require ACC approval.
items.rule:
All driveways must be constructed from an approved material type (pavers only). Any owner changing the appearance of a driveway, to include replacement must submit an application to the ACC for approval. No surface applications to driveways shall be permitted without the prior written approval of the ACC as to material, color and pattern. Such applications shall not extend beyond the front Lot line or include the sidewalk. Driveways need to remain free of grease, oil or other stains. Weeds growing through driveway pavers need to be eliminated. Driveways need to be kept free of debris. Driveway reflectors are not permitted.

All driveways should, if possible, permit a full size (20 foot) car to be parked in the driveway and not interfere with sidewalk access. Any change in size or shape of the driveway must be approved by the ACC. Extensions on either side of driveway may not exceed a combined total of four (4) feet, with approval. Only pavers are permitted to line either side of driveway.

items.title: Pressure cleaning needed
items.keywords: pressure clean wash mold mildew algae dirty roof sidewalk driveway house stained
items.observed: The [roof / exterior walls / driveway / sidewalk / lanai] at [location] is [stained / covered in mold, mildew or algae] and needs cleaning.
items.cure: Pressure clean the roof and exterior surfaces and pavement, including sidewalks and driveways, within 30 days of notice.
items.rule: Roofs and/or exterior surfaces and/or pavement, including but not limited to sidewalks, driveways, houses, or lanais shall be pressure cleaned within thirty (30) days’ notice by the ACC. Homes shall be repainted within forty-five (45) days of notice by the ACC.

items.title: Weeds in landscape beds / planters
items.keywords: weeds weed weeding landscape bed beds planter planters flower bed flowerbed garden mulch overgrown unweeded unsightly growth
items.observed: The landscape beds / planters at [location] contain weeds or other unsightly growth.
items.cure: Remove the weeds and other unsightly growth from all landscape beds and planters, and keep them weeded and maintained.
items.rule: (a) General Standard. All Lots shall be landscaped in a manner that is harmonious, compatible, and consistent with the overall landscaping and general appearance of the community. Each Owner shall maintain the landscaping and yard area of the Lot in an attractive condition, free from harmful insect infestations, disease, weeds, underbrush, refuse, and other unsightly growth or objects. Landscape maintenance includes care of trees, shrubs, hedges, ground cover, annuals, turf grass, and irrigation systems.

items.title: Weeds in lawn / turf
items.keywords: weeds weed lawn turf grass yard weedy crabgrass dollarweed broadleaf lawn weeds weed free
items.observed: The lawn at [location] has weeds that are not under control.
items.cure: Remove the weeds from the lawn and keep it weed-free through regular weeding and lawn care.
items.rule: Turf must be maintained & trimmed in a professional looking manner. No Weeds: A good lawn is free of weeds or has them under control. Regular weeding and lawn care practices can prevent weeds from taking over.

items.title: Landscape change without approval
items.keywords: landscaping change tree removed planted bed ACC approval shrub removal
items.observed: A landscape change ([describe: tree added or removed / shrub or hedge over 3 feet planted / landscape bed changed]) was made at [location] without ACC approval.
items.cure: Submit an ACC application for the change, or restore the landscaping to its previous approved condition.
items.rule:
(c) Approval of Changes. 1. Changes to landscaping require prior written approval of the ACC, except as provided in this subsection.

2. Prior ACC approval is required to (i) add any Tree; (ii) add any Shrub, Hedge, or other Plant that will grow to a Height of three feet (3') or taller; (iii) relocate or remove any Tree (subject also to subsection (g)); or (iv) change the location, size, or configuration of a landscape bed.

3. Prior approval is not required to (i) plant annuals, or Plants that will not exceed two feet (2') in Height, within the original landscape bed areas ("minor landscaping"), provided they comply with this Section and are maintained in an attractive manner; or (ii) replace an existing Plant with the same species and a comparable size in the same location.

4. Owners planting annuals are responsible for their upkeep, including removal when they die.

5. The ACC shall act on a complete application within thirty (30) days.

items.title: Lawn maintenance / hard edges
items.keywords: lawn mow mowing grass clippings hard edge edging sidewalk weeds dead sod overgrown
items.observed: The lawn at [location] is [not regularly mowed / overgrown / not hard-edged along sidewalks, curbs and driveways / has dead or damaged sod / has grass clippings left on hard surfaces].
items.cure: Mow the lawn, hard-edge it along the sidewalks, curbs and driveways, remove grass clippings from driveway, sidewalk and street, and replace damaged or dead sod.
items.rule: (d) Lawns and Turf. Turf areas shall be mowed regularly and maintained. Lawns must be hard-edged along sidewalks, curbs, and driveways in front of the Home at all times. Grass clippings must be removed from driveway, sidewalk and street. Damaged or dead sod and ground cover shall be removed and replaced. See Section 4.05 Turf for more information.

items.title: Failing or dead plant
items.keywords: dead plant shrub failing dying brown yellow hedge replace
items.observed: [Plant(s) at (location)] are dead or failing (dead, lost 50% or more of foliage, predominantly brown or yellow, or no longer screening as required).
items.cure: Remove and replace each failing plant with a healthy plant of comparable type and size within 30 days of notice. If a plant is recovering from recent pruning, storm damage or transplanting, you may request up to 90 days for recovery.

items.title: Shrubs / hedges overgrown
items.keywords: hedge shrub overgrown pruning trimming height 48 inches front yard untrimmed
items.observed: [Shrubs / hedges] at [location] are overgrown or untrimmed and exceed the maximum height (48 inches in the front yard, 10 feet in side and rear yards) or encroach on a sidewalk, driveway or street.
items.cure: Prune the plants to the permitted height and shape and keep them off sidewalks, driveways and streets. Hedges over 3 feet must be pruned at least twice per year.
items.rule:
(f) Shrubs, Hedges, and Other Plants. This subsection applies to all Plants other than Trees. 1. Pruning required. All Plants shall be regularly Pruned and shall not be permitted to grow untrimmed or unmaintained.

2. Height limits.

o (i) In the Front Yard, Plants (including Hedges) shall be maintained at a maximum Height of forty- eight inches (48") (four feet (4')).

o (ii) In the Side and Rear Yards, Plants (including Hedges) may be maintained at a maximum Height of ten feet (10').

3. Hedge pruning frequency. Any Hedge exceeding three feet (3') in Height shall be Pruned at least two (2) times per year and more often as needed to remain in compliance.

4. Screening. A Hedge installed to screen an item shall be of a size, height, and spacing that will obscure at least 80% of the item at installation and fully shield the item within one year of planting, subject to the Height limits above.

5. Sight lines. Within ten feet (10') of the edge of any driveway or street intersection, Plants shall not exceed thirty inches (30") in Height, and no Plant shall obstruct the visibility of drivers or pedestrians.

items.title: Tree maintenance / dead tree / stump
items.keywords: tree dead damaged leaning topped topping stump support stakes hazard tree removal arborist
items.observed: [Describe: dead or failing tree / topped tree / tree supports left on more than 12 months / stump not removed / leaning or hazardous tree] at [location].
items.cure: Remove and replace a failing tree with an approved species within 30 days of notice (or submit a certified arborist evaluation within 30 days), remove tree supports after 12 months, and grind stumps and restore the area within 60 days of removal. A hazardous tree must be made safe immediately.
items.rule:
(g) Trees. 1. County requirements. Each Lot shall contain the number and type of trees required by Sarasota County Code and Ordinance. Refer to the Approved County Tree List for Trees of Special Significance.

2. Protected trees. Any hardwood or protected Tree requires prior written approval from the county, where required by the county code, before an application is submitted to the ACC. All removals shall comply with the county code and applicable Florida law.

3. Pruning. Trees shall be Pruned and maintained in a healthy condition in accordance with accepted arboricultural practice. "Topping" or other pruning that harms a Tree's health or natural form is prohibited and is treated as damage for purposes of subsection (e)(2)(v).

4. Tree supports. Tree supports are permitted for up to twelve (12) months after planting. After that period, supports shall be removed, including those on crooked trees. If a Tree's orientation has not corrected within twelve (12) months, the Owner shall replace the Tree. Tree supports shall be a neutral color (for example, no neon colors).

5. Damaged or Failing Trees. A Tree that is a Failing Plant shall be removed and replaced within thirty (30) days after written notice from the Association, unless extended under paragraph 6. Replacement Trees shall be of a species approved by the ACC and shall meet the minimum size, species, and quantity required by the applicable county code, so that the Lot continues to satisfy its required tree allocation.

6. Arborist evaluation. Notwithstanding subsection (e)(3), if an Owner believes a damaged Tree can recover, the Owner may submit a written evaluation from a certified arborist within thirty (30) days after notice. If the arborist certifies that the Tree is expected to regain a healthy, full appearance, the Reviewer may allow up to twelve (12) months for recovery, subject to periodic re-inspection. A Tree that is not showing substantial recovery by the end of that period shall be replaced within thirty (30) days. The Reviewer may also extend deadlines for good cause, such as a pending insurance claim or documented unavailability of replacement Trees.

7. Hazard Trees. Any Tree that is dead, split, leaning, or otherwise presents an imminent safety hazard shall be made safe or removed immediately, regardless of any recovery period, in compliance with the county code (including any emergency exemptions) and Florida law. The Owner shall notify the Association as soon as practicable.

8. Stumps. Stumps shall be ground or removed, and the area restored, within sixty (60) days after a Tree is removed.

items.title: Prohibited / invasive plants
items.keywords: invasive plant brazilian pepper melaleuca prohibited plants exhibit
items.observed: A prohibited or invasive plant ([species]) was observed at [location].
items.cure: Remove the prohibited plant. Invasive plants, including Brazilian pepper, melaleuca and any Category I species, are not permitted anywhere in Heron Landing.
items.rule: (h) Prohibited Plants. Invasive plants are not permitted anywhere within Heron Landing, including Brazilian pepper, melaleuca, and any species listed as Category I by the Florida Invasive Species Council, as updated from time to time.

items.title: Landscape edging
items.keywords: landscape edging bed edge tree ring plastic wood mixed styles
items.observed: The landscape edging at [location] [is missing / is not an approved type or color / is damaged or rising out of the ground / is inconsistent / lacks tree rings].
items.cure: Install or repair edging in an approved type and color (concrete curbing, stacked brick/block/rock, properly installed black rubber tube-type, terrace board or aluminum), consistent across the property, with tree rings. No edging between the grass and driveway pavers.
items.rule:
All landscape in the front of the house must have an edge and be approved prior to installation or removal of existing landscape. Trees must have tree rings (edging around tree). Edging must be maintained, specifically, edging must:  Have clean lines: The edges are sharp and well-defined, creating a clear separation such as between lawn and flower beds.  Have consistent height: The edging material must have a uniform height, giving a neat and orderly appearance  Be durable: The materials used are to be in good condition, without cracks, rust, coming out of ground, or display any other signs of wear and tear  Be well-integrated: The edging complements the overall landscape design, blending seamlessly with the surrounding plants, mulch, and other elements  Have smooth curves or angles: If the edging follows a curved path, the curves are smooth and flowing. If it’s angular, the corners are crisp and precise Approved edging for Heron Landing is: 1.) Professional installed concrete curbing in approved colors.. 2.) Stacked brick, block or rock edging in approved colors. 3.) Properly installed black rubber tube-type edging. Must be properly installed in ground and may not rise up. Improperly installed rubber edging will result in a violation letter. 4.) Terrace Board, in approved color. 5.) Aluminum Edging, in brown, black or bronze.

The following materials are not permitted as in landscape edging: any type of plastic, wooden, or wire, fencing. All edging types/style and color must be consistent across all visible areas of property. (I.E. mixed styles and/or colors are not permitted)

No edging of any type should be used between the grass and driveway pavers.

items.title: Bed coverings / mulch
items.keywords: mulch rock bed covering bare ground pine straw
items.observed: Landscape beds at [location] have [bare ground / less than a 2-inch layer of mulch or rock / a non-approved bed covering].
items.cure: Refresh beds with at least a 2-inch layer of approved mulch (cypress, pine bark or cedar in red, black or brown) or approved rock. Shells, crushed gravel, pea gravel and coral are not permitted. Refresh mulch at least annually.
items.rule:
All landscaped plants & trees should be planted with the appropriate topsoil, peat moss and fertilizer mixtures. No bare ground is acceptable. All shrubs, ground cover and tree beds shall have a 2" minimum layer of mulch or rock. Mulch is required to be refreshed at least annually.

ONLY the following types of cover are permitted as landscape bed coverings:

1. Mulch: cypress mulch, pine bark mulch, cedar mulch (approved colors: red, black, brown)

2. Rock: crushed stone, marble rock, river rock, beach pebbles, lava rock. No shells, crushed gravel, pea gravel, or coral shall be permitted.

No boulders are permitted without ACC approval.

items.title: Turf standards
items.keywords: turf grass lawn height weeds dead patchy bare st augustine artificial clumps
items.observed: The turf at [location] [is patchy or has bare areas / has weeds / is yellow or brown / is not mowed at 3-4 inches / has clippings / is not St. Augustine].
items.cure: Restore the lawn to the standards: healthy green St. Augustine grass, mowed at 3-4 inches, weed-free, pest and disease free, hard-edged, with no visible clumps of clippings.
items.rule:
Artificial turf will not be approved anywhere in Heron Landing.

Turf must be maintained & trimmed in a professional looking manner. The standards for a well-groomed lawn are as follows:

 Healthy, Green Grass: A well-maintained lawn should have lush, green grass. The grass should be even in color and not show any signs of yellowing or browning.  Uniform Growth: The grass should grow evenly throughout the lawn without any patchy or bare areas. Proper watering and fertilization contribute to uniform growth.  Mowed at the Right Height: The grass should be regularly mowed at the appropriate height of 3-4 inches. Mowing at the right height helps the grass stay healthy and better compete against weeds.  No Weeds: A good lawn is free of weeds or has them under control. Regular weeding and lawn care practices can prevent weeds from taking over.  No Pests or Diseases: A healthy lawn is generally free from pest infestations and diseases. Proper lawn maintenance and occasional inspections can help detect and address potential issues early.  Well-Defined Borders: Clear edges (hard edges are required) between the lawn and other landscaping features, such as flower beds and walkways, give the lawn a neat and tidy appearance.  Grass Type: Lawn should be St. Augustine (dwarf grass such as Palmetto is not allowed).  No clumps of grass clippings should be visible on the lawn or on hard surfaces.
